scheme_name: Ministry of Law – Digital Courts Innovation Challenge
overview: The Ministry of Law – Digital Courts Innovation Challenge is not explicitly mentioned in the provided evidence. The Department of Justice, under the Ministry of Law & Justice, implements schemes related to judicial reforms, infrastructure development for courts, legal aid, and action research studies. The evidence primarily details the 'Scheme for Action Research and Studies on Judicial Reforms' and associated guidelines, sanction orders, and administrative functions.
objectives: Promote research and studies on issues related to the National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms
Undertake action research, evaluation, and monitoring studies
Undertake capacity building for research and monitoring activities
Promote innovative programmes/activities in Justice Delivery, Legal Research, and Judicial Reforms
eligibility: Eligible implementing agencies include Indian Institute of Public Administration, Administrative Staff College of India, Indian Institute/s of Management, Indian Law Institute, National Law Universities, National Council of Applied Economic Research, National Judicial Academy, State Judicial Academies, and other reputed institutions working in the field of justice delivery, legal education, and judicial reforms. Government or Government aided Institutes/Organisations may also be allowed if found suitable by the Project Sanctioning Committee.
benefits: Financial assistance for action research, evaluation, monitoring studies, organizing seminars/conferences/workshops, capacity building, publication of reports/material, and promotion of innovative programmes/activities in Justice Delivery, Legal Research, and Judicial Reforms. Assistance is provided in instalments with at least 10% retained as final payment upon acceptance of the final project report.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided on agreed terms and conditions based on the project proposal submitted by the implementing agency. Assistance may be given in instalments, with at least 10% of the project cost retained for final payment after acceptance of the final report. The financial assistance is limited to actual expenditure incurred, subject to an overall ceiling (e.g., Rs. 25.00 lakhs under the 2013 scheme, extendable in exceptional cases).
grant_amount_per_entity: Rs. 25.00 lakhs (ceiling, relaxable in exceptional cases)
application_process: 1. Project proposals are invited by the National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms, Department of Justice from selected implementing agencies for identified subjects. 2. Proposals must include title, name of implementing agency, details of Principal Coordinator, objectives, methodology, duration with timelines, and detailed project cost break-up. 3. Proposals are placed before the Project Sanctioning Committee for consideration and approval. 4. Approved proposals are submitted to the Integrated Finance Division of the Ministry of Law and Justice for fund release approval. 5. Funds are released in instalments upon approval by the Integrated Finance Division. 6. Implementing agency must submit Utilisation Certificate as prescribed by the Department of Justice.
required_documents: Details of Principal Coordinator (Name, Designation, Research Experience)
implementing_agency: Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India
contact_details: Email: ckreejonia@nic.in (from 2017 order), Phone: Tel./Fax No. 23072146 (from 2017 order)
caveats: Financial assistance limited to actual expenditure incurred by grantee institution
Overall ceiling on financial assistance (e.g., Rs. 25.00 lakhs) may be relaxed only in exceptional cases where project scope is wide, sample size large, or duration long
At least 10% of project cost retained as final instalment upon acceptance of final report
Disputes decided by Secretary (Justice) and Mission Leader, National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms, Department of Justice
Implementing agency may be required to recuse from deliberations if proposing agency is Indian Law Institute or National Judicial Academy
